_about: The competency questions, as the communication ontology composes them.

CORE1.question: Which documents does $DOC cite, so a fact traced to it can be traced further?
CORE1.why: A citation chain is how a reader gets from an answer to the source that actually says it.

gaps.say: the document cites nothing on record

CORE2.question: Which documents does the corpus hold, and how old is each?
CORE2.why: Every fact cites a document; the list of documents is the honest extent of what the graph can know.

CORE3.question: Which tools are declared, on what do they act, and who is accountable for invoking them?
CORE3.why: OTO never invokes; a reader must be able to see what can be done, on what, and who answers for it.

PF1.question: Which products do we build: in which domain and value stream, at what stage, owned by which role or team?
PF1.why: The portfolio in one answer: what exists and where it stands.

gaps.say: a product nobody owns

PF2.question: Which objectives do we pursue this period, which products pursue each, and how is each measured?
PF2.why: Strategy is objectives with products behind them; an objective no product pursues is a wish.

gaps.say: an objective no product pursues

PF3.question: Which products depend on which, upstream or downstream, and for what?
PF3.why: A late upstream product is a risk to every downstream one.

PF4.question: Which capabilities does the portfolio need, which product provides each, and which has no product?
PF4.why: The gap between needed and provided is the portfolio's finding; nobody fills it by guessing.

gaps.say: a needed capability no product provides

PF5.question: What has no owner: which products, capabilities and objectives name no role or team?
PF5.why: An unowned thing is nobody's problem until it is everybody's.

PF6.question: Which teams exist, what does each own, with what mandate, and how is it reached?
PF6.why: Who to call, by team, before anything is on fire.

PF7.question: Where is the knowledge of $PRODUCT: its query store, its site, and the packs it is specified, designed and run with?
PF7.why: The lineage between levels: a reader follows the portfolio to the product's store and the packs that explain it.

gaps.say: the product has no published store on record

PF8.question: Which products are live, which are being built, and which are retired?

PF9.question: Which team does role $ROLE sit in, and who holds it?
PF9.why: A role's team is who to page when the holder is away.

PF10.question: Which lower objectives support $OBJECTIVE?
PF10.why: Strategic alignment: the tree under one objective.

PR1.question: What is $PRODUCT and why does it exist: its problem, vision, stage, domain and value stream, and the promises it offers?
PR1.why: The product is the root every other fact hangs off; a reader must get its reason for being in one answer.
PR1.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: the product offers no value proposition: nobody has said why it exists

PR2.question: Who owns $THING: which role, held by whom, with what mandate?
PR2.why: Ownership sits on a role, not a person, so it survives staff changes; a thing with no owner drifts.
PR2.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: no role owns it

PR3.question: Who is $PRODUCT for, and who is it explicitly not for: which personas, with what need, wanting which promise?
PR3.why: Journeys, requirements and value propositions all hang off a persona; an unnamed audience is a product for nobody.
PR3.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: no persona is recorded for the product

PR4.question: Which requirements serve which value proposition or objective, and what kind and priority is each?
PR4.why: A requirement that serves no purpose is scope creep; the link is what lets a builder say why.
PR4.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR5.question: How do we know $GOAL succeeded: which criteria measure it, with what metric, target and due date?
PR5.why: Success must be measurable before the work starts, or it is declared afterwards by whoever shouts loudest.
PR5.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: nothing measures it: success cannot be told from failure

PR6.question: What is in scope for release $RELEASE, and what is the release's date, state and horizon?
PR6.why: Scope is dated, so what was in the next release as of a past date stays readable.
PR6.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: nothing is in scope yet

PR7.question: What was explicitly excluded from release $RELEASE?
PR7.why: An exclusion is recorded, not silently absent, so a builder does not build it and a reader does not expect it.
PR7.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR8.question: What is $PRODUCT made of: which features, realising which requirements?
PR8.why: Features nest through part_of, so an epic and a sub-feature are the same class; the map is read from the product down.
PR8.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: no feature is recorded as part of the product

PR9.question: How does a user get value with $JOURNEY: its trigger, its steps in order with their action and outcome, and its outcome?
PR9.why: A journey is how a persona gets value end to end; a step has its own identity so a decision or a test can point at it.
PR9.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: the journey has no steps

PR10.question: Which journeys exist for $PERSONA?
PR10.why: A persona with no journey gets no value the product can show.
PR10.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR11.question: What constraints is $THING built under, of what kind, imposed by whom?
PR11.why: A constraint is imposed from outside; forgetting one is how a plan becomes impossible late.
PR11.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR12.question: What assumptions does $THING rest on, and in what state is each: unverified, validated or invalidated?
PR12.why: An invalidated assumption means what rests on it must be revisited; the link is what finds it.
PR12.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR13.question: What are the risks and external dependencies: which risk threatens what, of what kind, in what state, mitigated by what?
PR13.why: The risk register must be readable from the graph alone.
PR13.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR14.question: Which open risks have nothing mitigating them?
PR14.why: An open risk with no mitigation is a decision nobody has made yet.
PR14.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR15.question: What did we decide about $THING, when, why, and whose call was it?
PR15.why: A decision settles what it is about, so nobody reopens it by accident; without the record it is reopened every month.
PR15.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: nothing has been decided about it

PR16.question: What is still open: which questions are unresolved, since when, and what are they about?
PR16.why: An open question is work somebody owes; the list must be readable without a search.
PR16.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR17.question: Which decision resolved $QUESTION?
PR17.why: A question is closed by a decision, or dropped; never by silence.
PR17.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: marked resolved with no decision on record

PR18.question: Which open questions block a release that has shipped?
PR18.why: A release should not ship with an unresolved question blocking it; one that did was shipped by accident.
PR18.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR19.question: Which document says so: where is $THING written down, in what kind of document, dated when?
PR19.why: Every answer must lead to a document a reader can open and judge for currency.
PR19.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: no document is recorded for it

PR20.question: What are we trying to achieve: which objectives does $PRODUCT pursue, for what period, in what state?
PR20.why: Objectives are where a product sits in the strategy; without them every feature is equally urgent.
PR20.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: the product pursues no recorded objective

PR21.question: Which lower objectives support $OBJECTIVE?
PR21.why: Strategy is the tree of objectives supporting objectives.
PR21.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR22.question: Which roles must be consulted or informed about $THING?
PR22.why: A stakeholder left out of a decision relitigates it.
PR22.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR23.question: What exactly must $THING do in each situation: which scenarios exercise it, given what, when what, then what?
PR23.why: A scenario is what a test verifies and what a builder implements; a requirement without one is a wish.
PR23.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: no scenario exercises it: nothing says how to test it

PR24.question: Which rules must $THING obey: which policies apply, of what kind, under whose authority, enforced by which role?
PR24.why: The governance edge: from here, a policy is enforced and a breach is attributable.
PR24.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

PR25.question: What does $TERM mean here, and what does it name?
PR25.why: A word with a definition, cited and dated, so a changed meaning is a supersession and not a surprise.
PR25.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-06 (the Gate 1 list this question runs)

gaps.say: the term names no entity; it is a definition only

PR26.question: Which decisions govern $THING, since when, decided by whom, and are they current?
PR26.why: "Why is this the way it is?" is answered by the decisions that shaped it; a superseded one is history, shown as of its date.

SA1.question: Which components make up $SYSTEM, and where does each run?
SA1.why: An incident starts from a system; the responder needs its parts and their environments in front of them.

gaps.say: no component is recorded as part of the system

SA2.question: Who owns $ASSET: which team do I call?
SA2.why: Ownership is the first question in every incident and every change; an asset nobody owns is nobody's problem.

gaps.say: no team is recorded as owning it; the system it is part of may be

SA3.question: Which interfaces does $COMPONENT expose or consume, and at what URL? If one changes, who breaks?
SA3.why: Coupling lives in interfaces; the blast radius of a change is read from exposes and consumes.

SA4.question: Which components write to $STORE?
SA4.why: A store with an unknown writer cannot be migrated or retired; two writers to one store is a design smell worth seeing.

gaps.say: nothing is recorded as writing to it: the writer is unknown

SA5.question: Which components read from $STORE?
SA5.why: Readers are who breaks when the schema changes.

SA6.question: Which components run nowhere on record?
SA6.why: A component with no environment cannot be found at three in the morning.

SA7.question: Which capabilities does $SYSTEM enable: what does the business lose if it is down?
SA7.why: The only question a non-engineer asks of the estate; the capability is the business's name for what the system is for.

gaps.say: no capability is recorded for the system

SA8.question: Which requirements does $ASSET satisfy?
SA8.why: A stated need must be traceable to the thing that meets it, or nobody can say whether it is met.

SA9.question: Why is $ASSET the way it is: which recorded decision shaped it?
SA9.why: A decision nobody can find is re-litigated; the record is what stops that. The decision is the product's: one record of why.

gaps.say: no decision is recorded about it

SA10.question: What is fragile: which risks threaten which assets, and what mitigates each?
SA10.why: The risk register must be readable from the graph alone, with the mitigation beside each risk. The risk is the product's, widened to the estate.

SA11.question: Which risks have nothing mitigating them?
SA11.why: An unmitigated risk is a decision somebody has not yet made; it must be visible until it is.

SA12.question: How do I operate or recover $ASSET: which runbook?
SA12.why: The runbook is the answer at three in the morning; the graph must hand it over without a search.

gaps.say: no runbook is recorded for it

SA13.question: Where is $ASSET written down?
SA13.why: Every answer must lead to a document a reader can open.

gaps.say: no design, review or standard is linked to it

SA14.question: Where is the code for $COMPONENT: which repository, owned by whom, on which default branch?
SA14.why: A tool on a component starts from its repository; the repository's identity must be data, not a guess.

gaps.say: no repository is recorded for it

SA15.question: What replaced what: which decisions, interfaces, components or systems were superseded, and by what?
SA15.why: A supersession is how the estate changes without losing what was true before.

SA16.question: What does $COMPONENT depend on, so a change to the provider is checked against the consumer?
SA16.why: Dependencies are where a change propagates; the graph must say what needs what.

SA17.question: Which requirements of the product does nothing in the design satisfy yet?
SA17.why: The trace from specification to design, read backwards: a requirement no system, component or interface satisfies is open design work, and the build must not start from it.

WK1.question: What is planned for $MILESTONE: which items, delivering which requirements and features, assigned to whom, in what state?
WK1.why: The plan for one date, with what each item makes true.
WK1.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

gaps.say: nothing is scheduled in it

WK2.question: What is $TEAM working on, and what of it is blocked, why, and waiting on whom?
WK2.why: A team's load and its blockers, in one answer.
WK2.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK3.question: What blocks $ITEM: which items, risks, open questions or decisions, and who owns each?
WK3.why: A blocker is a thing in the graph with an owner; the lead asks the owner, not the team.
WK3.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK4.question: Which requirements in scope of $RELEASE has no work item delivering?
WK4.why: A requirement in scope that nobody is working on will not ship.
WK4.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK5.question: Which requirements slip if $COMPONENT is late: the items that build it, the requirements it satisfies, the releases they are in scope of?
WK5.why: The question that crosses every level: the plan, the estate, the specification, the release.
WK5.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

gaps.say: the component satisfies no requirement on record, so nothing slips that anyone can name

WK6.question: Which items are overdue: due date passed, not deployed?
WK6.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK7.question: Which decisions is work waiting on, and whose call are they?
WK7.why: An open question or an untaken decision that blocks work has a deciding role; name it.
WK7.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK8.question: Which deployed items deliver a requirement nothing in the design satisfies yet?
WK8.why: Trace closure: deployed means the requirement is satisfied by something in the design, or the item was not what it claimed.
WK8.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK9.question: Which milestones are planned, when, owned by whom, and were they reached?
WK9.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK10.question: Which items must be done before $ITEM, and what is their state?
WK10.why: An item's own prerequisites: the critical path, one hop at a time.
WK10.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-10-07 (B6, the delivery lead's questions)

WK11.question: What is blocked: since when, why, and on whom?
WK11.why: The board's first column and M6's input: every block with its reason and whom or what it waits on, so the lead asks that person, not the team. One query, as the roadmap asks.

WK12.question: What is deployed, and where?
WK12.why: Deployed per environment is the plan's progress: qa, preprod, prod. Prod is done.

WK13.question: Where is $ITEM now: its state, set when, by whom, to which environment?
WK13.why: The current transition is the item's state with its provenance; the superseded ones, read as of a date, are its history.

CM1.question: What waits for $PERSON: pending messages, from whom, about what, since when, due when?
CM1.why: What a session opens with (N3): the messages addressed to this person that nobody has answered, each with its item.

CM2.question: What has been said about $ITEM, by whom, to whom, what was answered, and is it settled?
CM2.why: An item's conversation beside the item: who asked whom what, and whether it was resolved.

CM3.question: Which messages are overdue: due date passed, not resolved?
CM3.why: An unanswered request past its date is where the plan is stuck.
